title: Apache Spark vs Apache Flink: which should you use?
abstract: For most teams, Apache Spark™ is the better choice. Spark runs batch ETL, SQL analytics, machine learning and streaming on one engine, and Real-Time Mode now brings Spark streaming to millisecond, end-to-end latency. Apache Flink is a stream-native engine that fits specialized event-processing workloads, but choosing it usually means running a second engine next to Spark. The latency gap used to be the main reason teams added Flink. With Real-Time Mode, that reason has largely gone away, and the real question becomes how many engines you want to build, operate and govern. Spark is a unified engine for batch, streaming, SQL and AI, and Flink is a specialized stream processor. Both are open source Apache Software Foundation projects with exactly-once processing, stateful operators and SQL APIs. The difference is scope. Spark started as a batch engine and added Structured Streaming , which treats a stream as a table that keeps growing. The same DataFrame and SQL code runs as a scheduled batch job, a micro-batch stream or a Real-Time Mode stream. Flink was designed for streaming first and treats batch as a bounded stream. This table compares the two engines on the dimensions that usually decide the choice. Table 1. Apache Spark and Apache Flink compared. Sources: Apache Spark Real-Time Mode docs , Apache Flink 2.0 release and Flink CEP docs . In Databricks' published benchmark, Spark Real-Time Mode matched Flink on stateless work and had lower p99 latency on stateful aggregation and stream-static joins. The benchmark code is public, uses customer-derived feature-computation workloads and runs at 10,000 records per second for 30 minutes, measuring Kafka input-to-output latency. Databricks summarized the results as up to 92% faster than Flink . How to read these numbers: Databricks ran the benchmark. Spark ran on Databricks and Flink ran on AWS Managed Service for Apache Flink 1.18. The results compare Spark's worst run with Flink's best run. Treat them as evidence for these workload patterns, and test your own pipeline before deciding. Production results tell the same story. MakeMyTrip considered Flink, chose Spark Real-Time Mode to avoid a second engine and cut P50 latency to 44 ms and P99 from more than a minute to about 500 ms. Coinbase and DraftKings also run Real-Time Mode in production. For how the engine achieves this, read Breaking the microbatch barrier . You change the trigger. Real-Time Mode is a trigger on an existing Structured Streaming query, so the same code moves between latency tiers without a rewrite. Real-Time Mode needs update output mode and reads from and writes to Kafka or a row-level foreach sink. Stateful operators arrive in open source with Apache Spark 4.3 and are generally available on Databricks today. On Databricks, it runs on classic compute or in Lakeflow Spark Declarative Pipelines . See the Real-Time Mode reference for the full support matrix. Flink can be the better fit for a small set of specialized streaming workloads. Consider it when most of these are true: If the stream also feeds analytics, ML features or lakehouse tables, Spark avoids duplicating logic, operations and governance across two engines. Every second engine adds a second codebase, a second skill set and a second set of governance rules. Teams that pair Spark for batch with Flink for streaming often rewrite the same business logic twice and debug drift between them. Pipelines can also be declared instead of hand-wired. Spark Declarative Pipelines manage dependencies and incremental refresh for streaming tables. Databricks was founded by the original creators of Apache Spark and runs Real-Time Mode as a generally available feature, including stateful operators and transformWithState . It adds Lakeflow Spark Declarative Pipelines, Unity Catalog governance and serverless pipelines. Code written for open source Spark runs on Databricks unchanged. To get started, follow the Apache Spark tutorial: Real-Time Mode . In Databricks' published benchmark, Spark Real-Time Mode matched Flink on stateless workloads and had lower p99 latency on stateful aggregation and stream-static joins. Results depend on the workload, so benchmark your own pipeline. Not only. Spark Structured Streaming defaults to micro-batch, and Real-Time Mode processes records continuously with millisecond latency. You choose per query by setting the trigger. For most workloads, no. Real-Time Mode gives Spark millisecond latency on the same engine you use for batch, SQL and ML, so you run one system instead of two. Flink can fit specialized workloads such as very large keyed state, complex event processing or teams that already run a Flink platform for standalone streams. Yes. Most Flink SQL and DataStream logic maps to Spark SQL and DataFrames in Structured Streaming, and Real-Time Mode covers the low-latency path. Start with stateless and aggregation jobs, then move stateful logic to transformWithState. title: OpenAI and Databricks: Enterprise AI on your governed data
abstract: Greg Brockman, co-founder and President of OpenAI, has a simple way to describe AI without company data: “it's like hiring someone with 20 PhDs and never inviting them to a meeting.” Enterprises want to use frontier OpenAI models on the business data they already govern in Databricks, and they want to roll AI out to far more of their employees. OpenAI and Databricks formed their partnership to make that possible. OpenAI builds the frontier models, Codex, and ChatGPT that people use every day. Databricks provides the context those tools need to work inside a company: governed data, business definitions, and access rules. Genie Ontology is the context layer in Databricks that holds those definitions and shows how the company's data fits together, so ChatGPT using Genie knows what “revenue” or “active customer” means at your company before it starts working. Ali Ghodsi, co-founder and CEO of Databricks, and Greg Brockman, discussed the shift from chatbots to autonomous agents, and what enterprises need to get real value from them, in a conversation released earlier this week. You can watch it below. Most companies start with OpenAI and Databricks in one of three ways: Historically employees who needed numbers to make decisions couldn’t write SQL, so they looped in analysts or pasted data into AI tools that didn't know the company's definitions. Waiting on analysts slowed decisions down, and answers built on the wrong definitions led to the wrong decisions. Now, they can ask these questions themselves in ChatGPT using the Databricks Genie plugin. This lets a product manager ask questions like, “How is weekly active user adoption tracking against target by plan tier?” ChatGPT will use Genie to understand the company’s metric definitions, find the relevant data, run the query in Databricks and return results back in visual graphs and charts. The plugin runs on the Genie MCP . Where once decision-making was slow, now employees can act quickly and with greater confidence in the underlying data. Genie uses Genie Ontology, the context layer in Databricks that stores a company's approved metrics, business definitions, and how its data fits together. Genie applies the company's own definitions, so revenue in ChatGPT matches revenue in the finance reports. Users only see data they already have permission to see, and each answer links to its sources in Databricks. Because ChatGPT has the business context from Genie Ontology, it can do more than answer. Users can ask ChatGPT Work for recommended next steps and who should be involved, share findings through Slack or email, and carry out the actions they approve through connected tools. To get started, install the Databricks Genie plugin in ChatGPT. AI coding agents usually spread one team at a time, and leaders lose track of who uses them, what they cost, and where code and data end up. Databricks Unity Gateway makes it easy to manage this rollout allowing a company to give OpenAI Codex to every engineer while keeping visibility and control. Developers use Codex as they do today. Codex signs in with a Databricks credential, the OpenAI key stays in the Gateway, and every request is logged. Engineering leaders set budgets, review spend by team, and pick which GPT model handles which task. To get started, install the Unity Gateway CLI and run ug codex. The steps are in Connect Codex to Unity Gateway . Agents that could change core business processes often stall before production, because the data they need sits behind strict security and governance rules. On Databricks, OpenAI frontier models run next to that data under Unity Catalog governance. When Databricks serves the model, there is no external API key to manage. Teams can build and evaluate agents in Agent Bricks, or write them with the OpenAI Agents SDK and deploy them as Databricks Apps. To get started, open your Databricks workspace, go to + New > App, and choose the Agent - OpenAI Agents SDK template. The agent quickstart walks through it. Behind the three patterns is one partnership. Here are the key facts, how the platform fits together, and the other integrations available today. OpenAI models, Codex, and ChatGPT connect directly to Databricks, and several Databricks products run on OpenAI models. Databricks gets early access to new OpenAI models, and OpenAI models lead on OfficeQA, a Databricks benchmark for real document work. ChatGPT is where employees ask questions and get work done, Codex is where engineers write and review code, and Databricks Apps hosts the custom agents and apps that teams build. OpenAI frontier models do the reasoning in all three. Databricks Model Serving runs GPT models next to company data, so teams can call them from SQL, notebooks, and agents without managing a separate API key. Unity Gateway routes every model request, sets budgets by team, and keeps an audit log. The Genie plugin answers business questions in ChatGPT and Codex and gives them the business context from Genie Ontology to act on: the company's definitions, its data, and each person's access rights. The Lakehouse stores company data under Unity Catalog governance, and Lakebase, a managed Postgres database, keeps memory and state for agents. The two companies have also built these integrations: We'll publish a separate post on each pattern over the next few weeks, with architecture details, setup steps, and customer lessons. Teams that already work in ChatGPT and Codex can start with the Genie plugin and Unity Gateway. Teams that build in Databricks can start with OpenAI GPT models there. The same Unity Catalog permissions and Unity Gateway cost controls apply in every case. OpenAI and Databricks work together so enterprises can use OpenAI models and tools on governed business data & context in Databricks. OpenAI provides GPT models, Codex, and ChatGPT, and Databricks provides the data platform and governance. Use the Databricks Genie plugin, which runs on the Genie MCP. A Databricks admin turns on Genie, and users then connect it to ChatGPT. Each person sees only the data they're allowed to see. Codex sends its requests through Unity Gateway instead of calling OpenAI directly. Developers sign in with a Databricks credential while the OpenAI key stays in the Gateway. Leaders can set budgets and see spend by team, and every request is logged. Yes. Agent Bricks lets you build and evaluate agents, or you can also write agents with the OpenAI Agents SDK and deploy them as Databricks Apps. No external API key is needed when Databricks serves the model. Databricks serves recent OpenAI GPT models, including the GPT-6 family, and the open-weight gpt-oss models. The supported models list shows what's currently available. See the Databricks Genie plugin at work inside ChatGPT. Subscribe to our blog and get the latest posts delivered to your inbox.

title: FAA expands AI advice to manage air traffic congestion across entire US airspace
abstract: The US government has expanded the use of an AI tool for advising air traffic controllers to assist in managing air traffic across the entire national airspace system. Airline executives have voiced support for the rollout, but the US labor union representing air traffic controllers has said it was not involved in designing or testing the AI-driven system. The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) says the $875 million SMART system has helped reroute 180 flights since being implemented in airspace over Washington, DC, on September 21. The agency claims that this saved an average of 10 minutes per flight and almost 80 gallons of fuel per flight—and it is apparently hoping such results can be replicated nationwide through the expanded deployment. “After a successful initial rollout to the National Capital Region in September, the FAA will now use SMART in the airspace of all 22 centers across the country to reduce delays, reduce fuel consumption and improve the travel experience for the flying public,” according to the agency statement posted on November 10.

title: OpenAI board member worries an AI "takeover" of society could be months away
abstract: How do you think you're going to die? If you go by the current statistics for deaths in the US , it's reasonable to expect that cancer or heart disease will eventually get you. But OpenAI Foundation board member and Alignment Research Center Executive Director Paul Cristiano thinks we should all be worried about another major mortality risk. Speaking at a lecture series this week , Cristiano bluntly told the audience in a Toronto Convention Center, "I think for most people in this room, the most likely reason they will die is because of an AI accident." In the opening lecture of a three-part series , Cristiano outlined his worries about the risk of an impending "AI takeover." He defined that as a situation where goal-pursuing AI systems "call the shots in the same sense that humans today call the shots and what happens on Earth" and where any human trying to stop them "would be as ineffective as if you or me was trying to stop the US military." Such a situation would likely lead to mass death and perhaps uninhabitable environments for humans, Cristiano said.

title: Jensen Huang Resigns After Having Another Affair In Addition to the Chinese Spy
abstract: Jensen Huang has resigned as CEO of Nvidia and left its board. CFO Colette Kress will be interim CEO . Here is a quick profile of Kress . Here is a look at some of the potential long term successors . There were a lot of efforts to bury the fact that Jensen Huang had an affair with a Chinese spy, and then even to bury his second affair as well, and to get everyone to ignore the obvious implications of this. Then the second affair was revealed with executive Kimberly Powell, who directly reports to him. Even then, many doubled down on defending Jensen Huang as CEO of Nvidia. The Nvidia board disagreed, and was preparing to oust CEO Jensen Huang prior to his resignation. This creates a tricky situation for Nvidia, given that Jensen Huang had over 50 direct reports and did not believe in succession planning, and also for the White House . It also creates a tricky situation for many in Silicon Valley, who have invested heavily in their relationships with Jensen Huang and in the idea that founders are as Gods. This post covers all related events since my initial post . If you haven’t seen it, this short AI video is obligatory , as is this one . The Daily Show has coverage of stage one. They weren’t being all that subtle, huh? Odd Lots had an essay on the Megaspeed scandal . As Tracy Alloway says, one simple takeaway is that Nvidia could have easily sold all these chips to Americans. Matt Levine has additional coverage . Derek Thompson summarizes this ‘insane scandal.’ And of course , right on schedule: Nate Silver : I think, because it happened on top of the midterms and the midterms were a huge story, people are still underindexing on how seismic the NVIDIA story is. Especially when you read the deeper reporting on it. Rob Miles : I felt a little bit bad about attacking Jensen Huang in the past, but now I feel a lot better about it. I was probably still wrong, since I went from “This guy’s decisions and arguments seem surprisingly bad” to “Maybe he’s not as smart as people think he is” instead of “Maybe he’s compromised”. Chalk one up for Conflict Theory I guess… Nathan Calvin : Hey maybe NVIDIA’s PR person was telling the truth when he said that Jensen’s relationship with Alice Huang was neither unusual or unexpected. Bloomberg TV: In the interview, Huang said that his interactions with her were typical of those with Chinese customers and executives. To what one would hope would be the surprise of absolutely no one, Jensen Huang turned out to be having at least two affairs. In any sane world an undisclosed affair with a direct report is a lot less terrible than an affair with a Chinese spy. It is still quite bad. In America, this is still a sufficiently large breach of conduct that CEOs often get fired for it on its own. The other question is, now that the second ant has been spotted, how many more ants were there in this kitchen? It would be surprising if the count stopped at two. Ryan Mac, Tripp Mickle and Georgia Gee (NYTimes): Jensen Huang, the leader of Nvidia who is under investigation for an affair with a woman who U.S. intelligence determined is a Chinese spy, also had an extramarital relationship with [Kimberly Powell, Nvidia’s vice president of health care], an executive who reports to him, according to five people who worked at the company. … Mr. Huang, 63, and Ms. Powell, 48, were captured on video being affectionate at a San Jose, Calif., hotel during a Nvidia conference in March, according to two of the people who worked at the company. The New York Times has not seen the video. Both Mr. Huang and Ms. Powell are married to other people. … Mr. Huang’s relationship with Ms. Powell has been discussed inside the company, the five people said. … Mr. Huang is among a long list of chief executives of American companies who have had relationships with subordinates. Brian Krzanich resigned in 2018 from Intel, the chip maker, after acknowledging a “past consensual relationship” with an employee. Yes, according to Reuters, there was a third ant in the kitchen , another employee. There is not yet any word of what Ms. Huang will choose to do about all this. The Nvidia board had hired the law firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz to conduct its ‘independent investigation.’ Once the second affair was revealed, they were not going to wait for the investigation or try to bury the situation. Jensen was on his way out, and has now resigned. We still eagerly await the results of the investigation, for other reasons. This is 2026, so only after the second affair could we be sure that was how this would turn out, and even then there were people trying hard to defend him. It really, really should not have required the second affair. These quotes come from before the revelation of affair number two (of N): Andrew Curran : North Dakota Senator Kevin Cramer is calling for Jensen Huang to step down , and says that his actions ‘pose a clear national security risk.’ Gabby Miller (Politico): “The potential for extortion is so tremendous that something as sensitive as Nvidia chips, I just think he’s got to go,” Cramer told POLITICO late Tuesday. “If the worst thing he did in real life is infidelity with this woman who may or may not be a Chinese spy — but she might be — that’s enough, because whatever else there is, we don’t know. And to me, that’s a security risk.” … Gabby Miller (Politico): “Step down Mr. Huang, right now,” Kudlow said on the financial and economic affairs program he hosts on Fox Business Network, characterizing such a move as a “commonsense action.” Yes. Obviously. You fall on your sword, as Jensen Huang was forced to do. This was a good statement from the Select Committee on China : Megaspeed may only be the secondary scandal. The primary scandal could be Shanghai Century Litong, which became the central supplier to Chinese companies and facilitated at least $7.5 billion worth of Nvidia chips. The timeline and circumstances strongly suggest that Century Litong was able to do this, and get status as a preferred Nvidia customer shortly after being founded, through the influence of Alice Huang, despite her having zero AI background. As Rob Wiblin says, this is all pretty crazy. We know national security was compromised, and now we know one of the major ways that this happened . Jing Yang: Alice & Jensen have known each other since at least 2023. By 2023, when Alice launched her chip biz with no prior background in tech, she quickly established her credibility by boasting her chuminess with Jensen. She told people that Jensen celebrated her birthday every year. How exactly did the two Huangs met? We find out that Alice’s husband Kang Wei 康偉 got to know Jenson in the 2010s through gaming businesses. The Information Staff: The two have built a rapport that facilitated the shipment of at least $7.5 billion worth of Nvidia chips through Chinese companies since then, according to two people who know her. Alice Huang, her sister and her husband have built a labyrinth of companies spanning China and Singapore to acquire Nvidia chips, according to the people who know Alice Huang and corporate registration records. At the center of that corporate network is Shanghai Century Litong, a China-based company that was founded in June 2023 and, by October, was added to Nvidia’s list of preferred cloud partners, a status that comes with priority access to Nvidia’s chips. Four months after Century Litong was established, its major shareholder, listed in Shanghai Stock Exchange, disclosed that Century Litong had earned the credential as an Nvidia preferred partner for cloud services—a designation it continues to hold, according to Nvidia’s website . … Century Litong’s addition to Nvidia’s preferred list couldn’t have happened at a better time. … Century Litong’s clients were China’s largest technology companies, which cannot buy restricted Nvidia chips themselves. That made the company the go-to supplier for Chinese tech firms racing to develop their own AI systems.

title: [AINews] Jensen Huang resigns after 33 years leading NVIDIA
abstract: Congrats to Gemini 4 Hydrogen on their launch and it seems Anthropic’s IPO is well under way, but today’s headline was only ever going to be about one thing, the most earthshaking leadership change in AI (after Demis/Jeff/et al at Google DeepMind). Following news of a second affair , today NVIDIA announced his resignation (correlation/causation is debatable here), presumably forced by the board: There is also some discussion of the extent that Chinese models can demonstrably be shown to be trained on Blackwell GPUs that they should not have access to… though the scale is debated . Gemini 4 Hydrogen: Google's Fast Gemini 4 Tier Ships Broadly Launch : Google DeepMind released Gemini 4 Hydrogen, a speed-first model positioned alongside Carbon and Argon. Google says it completes tasks 2.5x faster than Gemini 3.8 Flash and edges Argon on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, 51 vs 50 at default thinking and 54 at the new xhigh level ( DeepMind , Koray Kavukcuoglu ). Specs and pricing : The model offers four thinking levels (low, medium, high and xhigh) and a 1M context window. It costs $1.50/$7.50 per million input/output tokens, with a 95% discount on cached input ( Phil Schmid , Artificial Analysis ). Official claims : Google reports 57% on Terminal-Bench 4.0 and more than 3x Gemini 3.8 Flash on Terminal-Bench 4.1. It also claims more than 5x fewer fabricated claims, #1 on Vals Tax Agent Bench and leading results on AutomationBench-AA and Agents' Last Exam ( Google ). Availability : Hydrogen is available on all Gemini API tiers, including a free tier in AI Studio. It is the default model in Search AI Mode, and free Gemini app users get it through auto-selection. Paid Pro and Ultra subscribers can use it in Antigravity ( Sundar Pichai , GeminiApp , Search ). Orchestrator multi-model mode : In Antigravity, Carbon plans while Hydrogen writes and tests code. Google says this reaches near-Carbon success on Terminal-Bench 4.0 with 24% less quota and 19% faster completion. It is rolling out to Ultra subscribers ( Google , Mohan ). Artificial Analysis measurements : The independent results show a mixed profile. Intelligence and cost : At xhigh, Hydrogen scores 54, one point behind Claude Sonnet 5.5 (max) and GPT-6.1 Sol (max). Its cost is about 32% of Sonnet's but about 2.5x Sol's. Cost per task is $3.16 at xhigh and $1.87 at high. Output speed is about 200 tok/s ( AA ). Strengths : Hydrogen has an 8% hallucination rate on AA-Omniscience, versus 43% for Sonnet and 52% for Sol. It also shares the #1 score on GDP.pdf visual reasoning. Weaknesses : It scores 54% on Terminal-Bench 4.0 at both high and xhigh, below Sonnet at 64% and Sol at 56%. Agent Arena : Hydrogen debuts at #5 with +14.8% net improvement across 6.5k sessions. It is the fastest model in the top 10 at 5.3 minutes per task median, with a median cost of $1.6 per task ( Arena ). Code Arena WebDev : It ranks #10 with 1703 points ( Arena ). Vals Index : It is #6 at 68.5%, 2 points behind Carbon at 38% of Carbon's price ( Vals ). Coding agents : CursorBench rises to 54.3% from 39.6% for 3.8 Flash ( Cursor ). Cognition's FrontierCode 2.0 shows 38.2%, just behind Sol ( Cognition ). SWE-sweep shows 13.5%, versus 9.5% for Astra ( KLieret ). Runaway reasoning : One tester saw xhigh spend 131K thinking tokens and about $1.08 without answering a jersey-number image question. The same tester reports budget exhaustion on 1.8% of a text benchmark ( skalskip92 ). Weak spots : Hydrogen scored 1% on MazeBench ( patience_cave ). Pricing structure : Simon Willison says Hydrogen is only a 25% discount on the Carbon/Argon token price, though those models reportedly double in price on Dec 1 ( simonw ). Speed : Theo disputes the "built for speed" framing based on his own timings ( theo ). Open-Weight Releases: Inkling 2 Small Leads Inkling 2 Small : Thinking Machines released the weights under Apache 2.0 ( thinkymachines , Mira Murati ). Size : It is a 594B-total / 17B-active MoE with text and image input and up to 1M context ( HF ). Architecture : New components include attention residuals with a q/k/v split, gated attention, a dynamic attention sink, dynamic shortconv and value norm ( Songlin Yang ). Experts use NVFP4 in layers 0–39 and MXFP8 in the last eight, with SWA widened to 1k and softcaps on the LM head and SwiGLU ( eliebakouch ). Day-0 serving : On vLLM, it fits on one GB200/GB300 node and reaches up to 630 tok/s per user at TP4. Its native DSpark speculator has an acceptance length of about 3.5 at T=1.0 ( vLLM , details ). SGLang reports 576 tok/s per user at batch 1 on Vera Rubin and text-plus-vision RL on 8 Blackwells ( SGLang ). SkyRL validates MXFP8, BF16 and LoRA RL ( erictang ). Evals : It is the #1 US open model on Code Arena WebDev at 1647 points ( Arena ). On Agent Arena it is #2 among open models, with a median cost of $0.26 per task ( Arena ). It also holds the top open-model spot on MathArena's BrokenArXiv ( MathArena ). Edge0-145B/120B : These are device-native open-weight models. The developer claims 86.5% on Terminal-Bench 2.1, versus 78.2% for Claude Opus 4.6, in about 29GB of memory at 75+ tok/s decode ( Samuel Zeng ). These figures are vendor claims. Perplexity Decider v1.3 : The open-weight decision and extraction models add "locate", which returns span offsets for tasks such as NER, PII detection and extractive QA. Perplexity says the release is 6.54 points more accurate than its production classifiers on 63 tasks, and the models are free on OpenRouter for one week ( Aravind Srinivas ). MiniMax H3-Image : It is the #1 open model on Multi-Image Edit Arena at 1365, tied with Nano Banana 2 and Pro ( Arena ). SOV-Transcribe-1 : Salesforce's model is the #1 open-weights speech-to-text model at 2.3% AA-WER, with 4.6B active parameters ( AA ). Checkpoint Forensics, Chinese Compute and Export Controls GPU fingerprinting claim : Will Depue says initialization patterns in released weights identify the GPU type that produced them ( report ). Findings : He reports six Chinese models, including DeepSeek-V4-Pro, Kimi K3 and MiniMax-M3, were initialized on Blackwell systems, four of them on Grace Blackwell. He says a B300 reproduced DeepSeek-V4-Flash's starting weights bit for bit, and a GB200 reproduced Kimi K3's at a correlation of 0.999995. Validation : He reports a 24-for-24 match on models with publicly disclosed hardware and match strengths of 49–1,385 sigma. He says Kimi K3's weights were created by at least 64 processes, all on Grace Blackwell ( rebuttal ). Scale estimate : He estimates 2–3K Blackwells each for the largest runs. He says senior OpenAI and Anthropic researchers verified the work but are not on record ( request for verifiers ). Scale : Critics say 2–3K Blackwells is about 6MW, a small fraction of China's roughly 24GW of installed compute. On that view, the result could indicate export controls are working rather than failing ( teortaxesTex , scale note ). Ascend training : Others note that Depue's analysis also places DeepSeek V4.1 Flash and LongCat on Ascend chips ( zephyr ). Novelty : Some researchers say Blackwell use by Chinese labs was already widely known ( eliebakouch ).

title: AI Ambition: ArtCraft Cloned Photoshop and Now Wants to "Rebuild Everything"
abstract: The theme of day two of the AI Engineer Code Summit in San Francisco was increasing ambition using AI . And there have been few projects as ambitious as ArtCraft in the AI era. So far the fledgling company has released 17 open source versions of popular software tools , starting with a Photoshop alternative built from scratch in Rust called PhotoCraft . You could feel the excitement in the room this morning when ArtCraft founder and CEO Brandon Thomas presented a kind of manifesto for AI-based open source at AIE Code. When he mentioned that ArtCraft had cloned Adobe’s Acrobat, with a product called PdfCraft, it got a round of applause from the audience. In wrapping up, his rallying cries of “let's take back the entire internet” and “let's rebuild everything” were greeted with whoops and cheers. Thomas began his presentation by reliving the internet’s early history. In his view, the web started out with the right intentions, but things got screwed up once Web 2.0 hit the mainstream. “We had a bunch of chat applications that were completely open,” he said, regarding the 1990s internet. “So, IRC is like Discord, but you can spin up your own servers that you actually own. You can use whatever programs to automate them and interrogate them without rules.” His point wasn’t necessarily that everything was open source, but that web users could freely build things. With Flash, for example — a commercial animation tool eventually acquired by Adobe — “kids were making all kinds of animations.” When Web 2.0 came along, with its superior broadband and smartphones, “it brought everybody into the fold.” Thomas acknowledged that this widened the scope of internet software, but at the cost of that freedom to build with leading apps. “The diffuse, experimental, early web started to disappear,” he said. “The APIs got taken away from us, and then we started seeing distribution being gatekept by the big providers.” It seems Adobe in particular annoyed Thomas. He described getting billed with an unexpected fee when he cancelled a monthly plan. “It's really frustrating that the web — that was once really, really promising and open and free — has turned into this extractive, owned, rent-seeking world.” This inspired him to start ArtCraft, “with the ethos of ‘let's build everything open source.’” A message even anti-AI people have gotten behind, according to Thomas. In addition to PhotoCraft, they’ve copied other apps in the Adobe suite, cloned Figma, and created a Microsoft-like word processor called WordCraft. There are also independent apps such as SolidCraft, a community-led CAD project distributed through ArtCraft’s launcher. Thomas reiterated that these AI-built applications are 100% open — “not only the desktop apps, but the actual infrastructure as well.” ArtCraft is starting with rewriting familiar tools. Thomas’s longer-term vision is for users (such as artists who were previously using Photoshop) to tailor the software to their own workflows. As he framed it, they want to “undo what had happened during Web 2.0 , when everything became owned and consolidated and gatekept, and just give people back their applications.” AI is the means to achieve that, he said. But aren’t there already open source alternatives to Photoshop, like GIMP? “GIMP isn't really used by artists,” said Thomas during his presentation. “We actually observed artists vibe coding their own workflows on top of the software that we gave them.” To begin creating PhotoCraft, the team gave an AI model a detailed prompt outlining Photoshop’s tools, data structures and file importers. After that, they “laid out a large, large prompt to say, let's build out the application.” As part of that process, they made everything MCP and CLI compatible . Within 24 hours, said Thomas, “we were looking at a pretty good approximation of what Photoshop was — and it kind of blew our minds away.” PhotoCraft interface; via ArtCraft website Thomas noted that PhotoCraft is “still not at 100% parity” — he said they’ve just passed 60% — but the team has set an internal goal to reach as close to 100% as possible. ( The project’s GitHub claims about 76% parity for feature breadth and about 46% for professional readiness.) “Right now, we want to fill the muscle memory of all the artists that use Adobe. So we are going for Adobe , their interface and ‘look and feel’ directly.” But after ArtCraft has achieved that, they plan to “build new apps that have new interfaces that are more agentic. ” Thomas said he was surprised by the amount of attention PhotoCraft, in particular, has gotten — ranging from the New York Times requesting an interview, to a swelling of its open source community to about 4,000 developers . “I'm still struggling to bear with what has happened. It struck a nerve with people. They felt sort of maligned by Adobe and other tech companies . And what we built has really resonated with them.” After his presentation, Thomas was mobbed by AIE Code attendees. ArtCraft’s apps are being downloaded at the rate of about 1.7 million per day, which Thomas said is still accelerating. In addition to the 17 official apps, there are around 300 being developed by the community, he added. Other than the AI technology, Thomas said that Rust was a crucial part of making the apps performant — he claimed that PhotoCraft opens ten times faster than Photoshop, for example. “Rust was probably essential in this product's success,” he said. “We've seen people do it in Electron before, but for high-quality creative apps, you really need something that's native. ” For those engineers who are not experts in Rust, Thomas has good news for you. “Do you need to know Rust to start using Rust today as an engineer? Definitely not. [...] Your agents will drive it just fine.” However, Thomas admitted that not everything has gone swimmingly. “We've run into a lot of gotchas — like permissions, GitHub, scaling, CI,” he said. “CI is falling over. We've been spinning up our own. We found a good place to get RAM on co-located servers.” But they have found an equilibrium on what agents can do and what needs to be handled by people. “If you're doing backend work or things that require schema migrations [or] API design, let your humans do that. But for desktop apps and games and anything that's basically immutable, throw your agents at it and give them full confidence.” And it turns out, there’s even an ArtCraft solution for you there. “AutoCraft is a completely autonomous software factory that we're going to open source.” There’s no doubting the ambition of Brandon Thomas and his ArtCraft company. “We can open source the entire world,” he proclaimed at the end of his presentation. “Let's own our apps, our infra, our protocols, our models — all of it.” It’s a big vision, potentially even on the scale of Linux if its current downloads growth rate continues. But, ironically perhaps, what intrigues me most about ArtCraft is the growth of its human contributor community. After all, that’s what the original web got most right: human collaboration at scale. The big difference from the 1990s is that now it’s agents doing the bulk of the development work.

title: The full DeepSeek App experience, now via API
abstract:
Search, files, links, safety, and voice. The capabilities behind the DeepSeek App are now available through the DeepSeek API.
Enable built-in features with a few parameters, or call standalone APIs such as OCR, ASR, and TTS. Build richer conversations or recreate the full DeepSeek App in your own application. Try our open-source frontend demo, with support for importing DeepSeek conversation history. 🔗 Demo: https://cdn.deepseek.com/chat-demo 📦 Code: https://github.com/deepseek-ai/chat-demo 📖 Details: https://api-docs.deepseek.com/guides/build_a_chatbot V4.1-Flash ( deepseek-flash ) now supports these capabilities across Messages , Responses , and Chat Completions , with tool calls and context assembly handled server-side: 🔹 Web Search: Search the web or images with citations in non-thinking mode. 🔹 Deep Thinking Search: Search and read pages throughout multi-step reasoning. 🔹 File Input: Parse PDFs, Office files, images, and more into conversation context. 🔹 URL Reading: Automatically fetch links in user messages to inform answers. 🔹 Safety Checks: Screen inputs and outputs, returning refusal indicators when risks are detected. Enable search with deepseek_web_search and URL reading with deepseek_read_url . Public-facing apps must enable safety checks. Developers remain responsible for content moderation, applicable model registration, and AI-generated content labeling. Search, Fetch, OCR, ASR, and TTS are also available as standalone APIs for custom workflows. Extended capabilities incur tool usage fees in addition to standard token charges.
See the tool pricing breakdown below. The DeepSeek App is just one way to interact with AI. Its capabilities are now yours to call and combine freely. Spend less time rebuilding the basics and more time creating something new. Build with DeepSeek. Let your imagination lead.

title: avenoxai/avenoxbeyin
abstract:
İkinci Beyin AI istemcin değişse de notların, kararların ve görevlerin aynı yerde kalsın. AvenoxBeyin, AI ajanlarınla kullanabileceğin yerel bir hafıza sistemi. Önemli bilgiyi Markdown dosyalarına kaydettirir, sonraki oturumda kaynağıyla bulursun. Klasörünü Obsidian'da veya istediğin metin editöründe açabilirsin. Kuruluma geç · Son sürümü indir · Görsel kurulum rehberi · Belgeler macOS · Windows · Linux   |   Python 3.11+   | MIT lisansı Ne işe yarar? İstediğin Beyin ile yapabileceğin Yeni oturumda kaldığın yerden devam etmek Son işin sonucunu, açık konuları ve sonraki adımı kaynak notlara kaydetmek Daha önce verdiğin kararı bulmak Notlarda aramak, kararın geçtiği dosyayı açmak Bir kaynağı kaybetmemek Video, makale veya dosyayı Yakala ile gelen kutuna almak Claude'dan Codex'e geçmek Aynı klasördeki not ve görevleri başka bir desteklenen istemciyle kullanmak Nasıl çalışır? flowchart TB
    A["Sen ve AI ajanın"] -->|"Bilgiyi kaydet"| B["Yerel Markdown notları"]
    B -->|"Yerel arama"| C["İlgili notlar ve kaynakları"]
    C -->|"Sonraki oturumda bağlam"| A Loading Asıl kaynak dosyaların. Beyin bunların yerel indeksini tutar ve seçilen bağlamı kullandığın AI istemcisine verir. Sohbet geçmişinin tamamını kendiliğinden bilgiye dönüştürmez; kalıcı olmasını istediğin şeyi nota yazdırırsın. V3.13.0'da yeni: Yakala'dan isteğe bağlı Claude/Codex'e gönderim, Word (.docx) belgelerini okuma, Pi bağlantısı ve OpenCode global köprüsü. Yerel web görünümü ve çalışma alanı araçları da bu sürümde. Tüm yenilikler . Üç adımda kurulum Gerekenler: Python 3.11+ ve desteklenen bir AI istemcisi. İstemcinin kurulumu ve hesabı ayrı gerekir. Beyin'in temel kurulumu için Git, pip, Mem0 hesabı, ek API anahtarı veya sürekli açık sunucu gerekmez. Obsidian isteğe bağlıdır. 1. Bir klasör seç Yeni bir klasör veya mevcut Obsidian vault'un olabilir. Notlarını başka yere taşıman gerekmez. 2. AI istemcinde o klasörü aç Claude Code, Codex veya aşağıdaki istemcilerden birini kullan. Kurulumu istediğin klasörde çalıştığından emin ol. 3. Bu mesajı yapıştır https://avenox.io/beyin.md adresini oku. Bu klasöre ikinci beynimi kur.
Mevcut kurulum varsa notlarımı koruyarak güncelle. Gerekli indirme ve
kurulum adımlarını sen yap. Sonunda örnek bir bilgiyi kaydedip yeni
oturumda geri okuyarak birlikte doğrulayalım. Ajan resmi kararlı paketi indirir, checksum'u doğrular ve kurulumu kontrol eder. İstemcinin gösterdiği klasör veya hook güven incelemesini tamamla. Ardından aynı klasörde yeni bir oturum aç ; Codex'te yeni hook tanımlarını /hooks ekranında incele. Terminalden kendim kurmak istiyorum Son sürümden beyin-v3-X.Y.Z.zip ve yanındaki .sha256 dosyasını indir. GitHub'ın Source code arşivini seçme. ZIP'in SHA-256 değerini yanındaki dosyayla karşılaştır ve paketi aç. Doğrulama adımları . Açtığın paket klasöründe terminal aç. Vault yolunu kendi not klasörünle değiştir: macOS / Linux python3 scripts/install_v3.py --vault " /tam/yol/Beynim " Windows py -3 scripts / install_v3.py -- vault " C:\Notlar\Beynim " Kurucu motoru, istemci bağlantılarını ve dört başlangıç skill'ini vault'a yerleştirir. Paket klasörünü açık tutman gerekmez. Vault'u istemcinde aç, güven incelemesini tamamla ve yeni bir oturum başlat. Ayrıntılı kurulum . İlk 5 dakika Ajanına sırayla şunları söyle. Bunlar örnek mesajlar; kendi bilgilerinle değiştirebilirsin. Adım Ajanına söyle Tanış “Beyin skill'ini kullan. Beni tanımak için birkaç kısa soru sor ve cevaplarımı notlara kaydet.” Kaydet “Örnek proje için Python seçtim, çünkü ekip Python biliyor. Bunu karar notu olarak kaydet.” Geri bul Yeni oturum aç: “Örnek projede hangi dili seçmiştik, neden? Kaynak notu göster.” Görev oluştur “Örnek projenin ilk taslağını hazırlamam için bir görev oluştur.” Kaydı dosyada, geri çağırmayı yeni oturumda kontrol et. Böylece kendi istemcinde bağlantının çalıştığını da görürsün. Kurulan dört skill ne yapıyor? Skill Kullanım beyin Not bulma, bilgi kaydetme, görev ve iş sonucu oluşturma beyin-doktor Bağlantı, kayıt ve kurulum sorunlarını kontrol etme beyin-guncelle Güncelleme, sürüm kontrolü ve geri alma beyin-kontrol Hafızadaki bilginin hala doğru olup olmadığını denetleme; yalnız sen istediğinde çalışır, onayın olmadan yazmaz Ortak kaynak .agents/skills içindedir; Claude ve Kiro kendi proje kopyalarını kullanır. Mevcut kişisel skill'ler sessizce ezilmez. Hangi istemcilerle kullanılır? İstemci Kurulum sonrası Claude Code Vault klasöründe yeni oturum aç. Codex Yeni hook tanımlarını /hooks ile incele; yeni oturum aç. Google Antigravity Vault'u workspace olarak aç ve klasöre güven. Kurulum Kiro Hook'ları incele; yeni oturum aç. Rehber Hermes Agent Profil bağlantısını yap, beyin-v3 eklentisini etkinleştir. Rehber OpenCode Vault klasöründe aç; eklenti yüklenir. Rehber OMP / Oh My Pi Vault klasöründe aç; hook yüklenir. Rehber Pi Extension için proje güvenini onayla; yeni oturum aç. Rehber DeepSeek Harness (DSH) Yalnız açık context / receipt CLI kullanımı; otomatik teslim doğrulanmadı. Rehber İstemcilerin hook ve güven akışları farklıdır. Codex Desktop'ta açık skill kullanımı ile otomatik hook teslimi aynı şey değildir; otomatik Desktop akışı henüz doğrulanmış sayılmaz. Gerçek istemci kontrolleri . Başka proje klasörlerinde çalışırken merkezi beynine erişmek için isteğe bağlı global köprü var. Bir kaynağı tek tuşla yakala Video, tweet, makale, mail veya dosyayı gelen kutuna al. Sonra ajanına “yakalananları işle” de; metni çıkarıp notlarına bağlasın. Bir kez, vault klasöründe: python3 beyin.py yakala kur macOS Windows Linux Control + Option + B Ctrl + Alt + B KDE Plasma'da Ctrl + Alt + B ; diğer masaüstleri için rehber Varsayılan Enter yalnız kartı kaydeder. İstersen Claude Code veya Codex ajan modunu ayrıca açıp Ctrl+Enter ile o kartı ajana gönderebilirsin. Word (.docx) belgeleri desteklenir; YouTube sesini yazıya çevirme gibi ek işler ayrı araçlar gerektirebilir. Yakala rehberi . Beynine tarayıcıdan bak Görevlerini, son iş sonuçlarını ve doktor özetini tek ekranda gör. İsteğe bağlı web görünümünü vault klasöründe aç: python3 beyin.py web ac Gerçek arayüz, örnek not ve görevlerle, salt okunur modda görüntülendi. Kişisel veri içermez. Yalnız bu bilgisayarda açılır; 30 dakika kullanılmazsa kapanır. Kurulum sırasında kendiliğinden başlamaz. Sadece görüntülemek için web ac --read-only kullan. Web rehberi . Güncelleme ve yardım Güncellemek için ajanına “beynimi güncelle” , sorun varsa “beyin-doktor ile kontrol et” de. Terminal tercih edersen vault klasöründe : python3 beyin.py update --check # Yeni sürümü kontrol et python3 beyin.py update # Güncelle python3 beyin.py doctor # Kurulumu ve bağlantıları kontrol et Windows: Bu sayfadaki python3 beyin.py ... komutlarında python3 yerine py -3 kullan. Yakala kullanıyorsan , güncellemeden sonra python3 beyin.py yakala kur komutunu bir kez daha çalıştır; ayrı kopyalanan dinleyici ve skill de yenilensin. İstemcinde yeni oturum aç. Global köprü kullanıyorsan sürümün yeniden kurulum notlarını da kontrol et. Kullanıcı notları güncellenen sistem dosyalarından ayrıdır. Yönetilen bir dosyada kendi değişikliğin varsa sessizce ezilmez; çakışma bildirilir. Çevrimdışı güncelleme, rollback ve recover . Merak edilenler Notlarım nerede? AI sağlayıcısına ne gider? Notların yerel Markdown dosyalarında, indeks bu bilgisayarda tutulur. Seçilen bağlam AI istemcine verilir; istemcinin model sağlayıcısı ve hesap koşulları geçerlidir. “Yerel hafıza”, bütün AI konuşmasının çevrimdışı olduğu anlamına gelmez. Özel not işaretleri Beyin'in bağlam ve web filtrelerini etkiler; dosya erişimi verdiğin bir ajan için işletim sistemi düzeyinde koruma oluşturmaz. Kaynak biçimi ve görünürlük . Ek maliyet veya sürekli çalışan bir servis var mı? Temel yerel kontroller model çağırmaz. Ajana yaptırdığın işler ve eklenen bağlam istemcinin normal tüketimine girer. “Ekonomik moda geç” veya “otomatik kontrolleri kapat” diyebilirsin; desteklenen istemciler aynı vault tercihini kullanır. İstemciler kapalıyken sürekli hafıza tarayan bir servis yoktur.
